text:
devon: Quick heads-up — my savings-plan/RI coverage vs actual GPU consumption is misaligned across regions for p4d. We have a decision window before the next renewal cycle.

amy: How big is the delta? percent or $ number?

devon: Short summary: ran a usage pull for Feb–Apr. Rough numbers: committed hours (us-west-2 p4d) = 7,200h, actual used ~4,200h (~58% utilization). eu-west-1 p4d used ~6,800h but committed ~2,000h (~340% demand vs commit). Net: we are overcommitted in us-west-2 and undercommitted in eu-west-1.

santiago: Oof. That explains the odd billing spikes when teams burst to premium instances. We can either: (1) modify convertible RIs where possible, (2) shift savings plan purchases across regions (if SP scope allows), or (3) rely on short-term on-demand/dedicated bursts while we rebalance.

maria: Biggest constraint is contractual for some reserved capacity (Dedicated pools for enterprise customers) — we can't move those. But for the general pool we have some wiggle room. What's the timeline on expirations?

devon: Expiries: ~40% of the p4d reserved capacity in us-west-2 rolls on 2026-06-15; another 30% in us-west-2 is auto-renewing month-to-month. eu-west-1 commitments are mostly annual and locked until 2026-12.

kai: Can you drop the raw query or runbook? I can script a migration/modify plan if we have the instance IDs and reservation IDs.

devon: Pasted query I used for the COE table:
```
-- simplified pseudo-SQL output from internal billing db
SELECT region, instance_family, reservation_id, committed_hours, used_hours, start_date, end_date
FROM commitment_usage
WHERE instance_family = 'p4d' AND month IN ('2026-02','2026-03','2026-04');
```
Results uploaded to S3: s3://infra-reports/commitment-audit/1923456789-p4d.csv (infra-bot attached).

infra-bot: Report generated and uploaded: s3://infra-reports/commitment-audit/1923456789-p4d.csv — presigned link valid 7 days.

amy: Nice. Can finance run the amortized cost delta if we exchange/modify vs let lapse? Prefer a simple $/token delta for Q3 budget planning. @santiago can you coordinate?

santiago: Yep. I will: (A) pull reservation modify feasibility (convertible RIs only), (B) run a model for buying a 1y targeted SP in eu-west-1 vs adding on-demand capacity in us-west-2, (C) include break-even points. ETA EOD Fri.

maria: Also add an operational risk note: if we move commit away from us-west-2 we need to ensure latency-sensitive customers in that region are covered by Dedicated or hotspot capacity. Otherwise product teams will complain.

devon: Agreed. Action items:
- Hold any auto-renew in us-west-2 for the June 15 chunk until we see Santiago's model (I put a calendar hold on the renewal job).
- Kai to draft reservation-modify script for convertible RIs and a checklist for finance to review.
- Maria to inventory Dedicated pools tied to contracts and flag non-movable units.
- Santiago to produce cost/delta model and recommended buy/sell/modify plan.

kai: I’ll start a PR with a script template + dry-run logs. Will link once ready. Example CLI snippet I’ll use for the dry-run:
```
aws ec2 describe-reserved-instances --filters Name=instance-type,Values=p4d* 
# then aws ec2 modify-reserved-instances --reserved-instances-ids <id> --target-config ... (dry-run)
```

amy: If we can get a short summary (1 slide) by Monday for GTM and Finance, that would be perfect.

santiago: Working on it. If we plan to convert any RIs, we need procurement sign-off — that will take time, so include that in timeline.

devon: Thanks all. I’ll leave the calendar hold and mark the renewal ticket as blocked for now. :white_check_mark:

maria: ack, thanks.

amy: thanks — appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:
